thread:
sophie: Hey team — BrightMetrics reporting a spike of autopay failures this morning. Multiple invoices failing with \"card declined - insufficient_funds\" but merchant sees different responses upstream. Customer says it started ~08:10 UTC, high latency on /v1/payments. Ticket: INC-4321 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4321)

payments-bot: New incident created: INC-4321. Assigned to support@redwood. :rotating_light:

leo: Can you paste a repro payload + idempotency key? Also what acquirer are they on? Any recent routing policy changes?

sophie: Repro curl from customer (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XYZ' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: bm-2026-03-17-001' \
  -d '{"merchant_id":"brightmetrics","amount":12900,"currency":"EUR","card":{"number":"**** **** **** 4242","exp_month":11,"exp_year":2028},"autopay":true}'
```

sophie: They see three attempts in a row, last two return decline. Customer attach logs: gateway returns code=RISK_REJECT, acquirer shows ACS timed out on attempt 2.

tanya: From a quick glance, gateway has a risk filter that converts some issuer RISK_REJECT -> insufficient_funds in our UI. But ACS being unreachable can also cause fallback to soft-decline path. Need trace IDs.

leo: Sophie — can you pull the trace id from the customer's API response headers (x-rw-trace) for one failed attempt?

sophie: Found: x-rw-trace: trace-00084bd2. Pushing logs now.

eng-ryan: Got the trace. I see a spike in our acquirer connector latency at 08:10:22 — TCP handshakes to ACS took >6s and then a 504 from acquirer. Our payment handler has a 5s acquirer timeout by default, so we aborted and routed to soft-decline. That explains the inconsistent upstream messages.

leo: Do we have evidence issuer marked it as FRAUD or just did not respond? Engine logs show issuer returned HTTP 200 with body {"action":"NO_CHALLENGE","reason":"ACS_UNAVAILABLE"} in attempt 2.

tanya: So behavioral flow: 1) initial auth attempted -> acquirer times out -> we fallback to risk path (RISK_REJECT) -> UI shows insufficient_funds. Not actual funds problem.

sophie: Customer is worried this is causing failed autopays and accounting mismatch. They want an urgent workaround — can we re-run the transactions or force a different acquirer for BrightMetrics?

eng-ryan: Short-term options:
- temporarily increase acquirer timeout to 8s for merchant brightmetrics (config flag)
- enable acquirer failover for their routing policy (route to secondary acquirer on timeout)
- disable strict risk-mapping for autopay route so we surface issuer reason instead of mapping to insufficient_funds

leo: I can flip the routing flag and increase timeout for them, but need ops approval. Also recommend requeueing the failed payments with a 30s backoff and idempotency key to avoid duplicates.

sophie: Ops approved on call. Leo, can you apply the routing change and requeue one invoice as a test? I'll coordinate with the merchant.

leo: Applying routing change now — toggled "use_acquirer_failover" for merchant brightmetrics. Also bumped acquirer_timeout to 8000ms for their namespace.

payments-bot: Config change recorded (CHANGE-99823) by leo at 08:42 UTC.

leo: Requeued invoice inv_2026_03_17_77 with same idempotency key. Will monitor.

sophie: Merchant confirmed a successful capture on the requeued attempt. They also asked for an explanation and an update to their SLA dashboard.

tanya: We should add a telemetry alert: if acquirer timeout rate >1% for 5m, auto-enable failover for affected merchants. I'll open an RFC.

eng-ryan: Agreed. Also long-term fix: evaluate connection pooling and route selection for that acquirer. Might need kernel tweaks on connector hosts.

sophie: I'll send customer summary and close INC-4321 after they confirm no other invoices failed. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

leo: Nice work. :thumbsup:

sophie: Filing follow-up RFC link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RFC-7260 — includes telemetry proposal.

payments-bot: Incident INC-4321 status -> investigating -> resolved (requeue success).
